_comment: v3.66.1232 row-189 battery. The census decides by EVALUATING a candidate expression, so the mutants are the ways evaluation can be quietly turned back into a spelling test or made to answer for everything. M4 is the over-correction: a census that reports every function is caught only by the clean-code control, which is why that control exists. FIRST RUN: 3 caught, 2 ESCAPED, both real. Nothing distinguished a census that had lost its DISCRIMINATING probes -- every clean-code control happened to also be clean under the reduced probe set -- and the population test rebuilt the file list itself instead of asking the scanner, so a scanner mutated to read nothing still passed. A constant-public-suffix control and a _LAST_SCANNED publication were added for them.
subject: v3.66.1232 -- the registrable-domain census judges the answer, not the spelling

mutants.label: M1 single-assignment aliases are no longer inlined, so  hides the rule
M2 f-strings drop out of the evaluable grammar, so one spelling escapes again
M3 the discriminating probes go, leaving only hosts where last-two is wrong
M4 one matching probe is enough, so any domain-shaped answer is an offender
M5 the drain scans nothing and reports clean
